# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- Chat bots that post messages over HTTP (see [bots](docs/bots.md))
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.
# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Chat bots

Bots are members of rooms that post messages over HTTP. A bot is set up by a chat member and then driven
by a shell script or CI job, which authenticates with the bot's code.

## Setting up a bot (people)

1. Open account settings (`/account/edit`) and click the bot icon, "Set up chat bots" (`/bots`).
2. "Add a chat bot" opens `/bots/new`. The bot name is required, the avatar is optional. "Save changes" creates
   the bot and returns to `/bots`.
3. Each bot on the list shows its name and its **bot code** in a read-only "Bot code" field. Copy it into your
   script or CI secrets. Treat it like a password.
4. "Edit <name>" changes the name and avatar. "Delete this chat bot" (with a confirmation) removes the bot.

Who sees and manages what:

- Any chat member can create bots. A member sees, edits and deletes only the bots they created.
- Administrators see and manage every bot.
- The bots page lists all of them on one page (no pagination).
- Bots are left out of the people list on the account page, since they're managed from `/bots`.

Bots join all open rooms, like any new person. They can be added to closed rooms the same way people are
(the access switches in the room's settings).

## Posting messages (bots)

The raw request body is the message. There is no JSON envelope and there are no field names:

```sh
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

| Response | When |
| --- | --- |
| `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:message_id` | The message was posted. |
| `422 Unprocessable Content` | The body is empty or only whitespace, or it isn't valid UTF-8. |
| `404 Not Found` | The room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it. |
| `401 Unauthorized` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bot realm="Campfire"`) | The bot code is unknown, the bot was deleted, or its user was deactivated or banned. |

Details:

- The body is text, whatever `Content-Type` the client sends. `curl -d` sends form encoding by default, and
  that doesn't change the message: `Disk at 100% done` is posted as written.
- Line breaks are kept. Markup is shown as text, so `<b>` in a message appears literally.
- Attachments aren't supported. The body is the whole message.
- The message shows the bot's name as its author. It's broadcast to the room, updates unread markers, and
  triggers push notifications exactly like a person's message.
- `Location` is `/messages/:id`, as specified. Messages are room-scoped in this app, so that URL returns 404
  today. A future change could resolve it to the room's message.

## Design notes

**Data model.** A bot is a `bots` row (`user_id`, `creator_id`, `bot_key`) that points at an ordinary `users`
row. The user holds the bot's name, avatar and room memberships, so everything that handles people (membership,
mentions, messages, push, avatars) works for bots without changes. The credential lives only in `bots`, so it
never appears when users are serialized or listed.

**Bot users can't sign in.** The `users.password_digest` column is `NOT NULL`, so a bot's user gets a random
password that nobody learns. A bot has no email address, and its profile doesn't offer the auto-login link.

**Deleting a bot** deactivates its user, the same way removing a person does: the user leaves every room (direct
rooms excepted), and its messages stay. The `bots` row is destroyed, which kills the bot code. Deactivated and
banned users fail authentication too (`Bot.active`).

**Posting.** `Bots::MessagesController` is unauthenticated by session and doesn't check CSRF tokens, because
the bot code in the path is the credential. Rails parses form bodies before any action runs, and it rejects
text such as `100% done` with a 400. The controller therefore declares the body as not being form fields
(`process_action`). `Bots::MessagesControllerTest` covers this.

**Authorization.** Editing and deleting use `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)`, which means administrator or
creator, the same rule used for other records here.

## Protecting bot codes

A bot code grants the ability to post as the bot, so:

# Chat bots

Bots are members of rooms that post messages over HTTP. A bot is set up by a chat member and then driven
by a shell script or CI job, which authenticates with the bot's code.

## Setting up a bot (people)

1. Open account settings (`/account/edit`) and click the bot icon, "Set up chat bots" (`/bots`).
2. "Add a chat bot" opens `/bots/new`. The bot name is required, the avatar is optional. "Save changes" creates
   the bot and returns to `/bots`.
3. Each bot on the list shows its name and its **bot code** in a read-only "Bot code" field. Copy it into your
   script or CI secrets. Treat it like a password.
4. "Edit <name>" changes the name and avatar. "Delete this chat bot" (with a confirmation) removes the bot.

Who sees and manages what:

- Any chat member can create bots. A member sees, edits and deletes only the bots they created.
- Administrators see and manage every bot.
- The bots page lists all of them on one page (no pagination).
- Bots are left out of the people list on the account page, since they're managed from `/bots`.

Bots join all open rooms, like any new person. They can be added to closed rooms the same way people are
(the access switches in the room's settings).

## Posting messages (bots)

The raw request body is the message. There is no JSON envelope and there are no field names:

```sh
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

| Response | When |
| --- | --- |
| `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:message_id` | The message was posted. |
| `422 Unprocessable Content` | The body is empty or only whitespace, or it isn't valid UTF-8. |
| `404 Not Found` | The room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it. |
| `401 Unauthorized` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bot realm="Campfire"`) | The bot code is unknown, the bot was deleted, or its user was deactivated or banned. |

Details:

- The body is text, whatever `Content-Type` the client sends. `curl -d` sends form encoding by default, and
  that doesn't change the message: `Disk at 100% done` is posted as written.
- Line breaks are kept. Markup is shown as text, so `<b>` in a message appears literally.
- Attachments aren't supported. The body is the whole message.
- The message shows the bot's name as its author. It's broadcast to the room, updates unread markers, and
  triggers push notifications exactly like a person's message.
- `Location` is `/messages/:id`, as specified. Messages are room-scoped in this app, so that URL returns 404
  today. A future change could resolve it to the room's message.

## Design notes

**Data model.** A bot is a `bots` row (`user_id`, `creator_id`, `bot_key`) that points at an ordinary `users`
row. The user holds the bot's name, avatar and room memberships, so everything that handles people (membership,
mentions, messages, push, avatars) works for bots without changes. The credential lives only in `bots`, so it
never appears when users are serialized or listed.

**Bot users can't sign in.** The `users.password_digest` column is `NOT NULL`, so a bot's user gets a random
password that nobody learns. A bot has no email address, and its profile doesn't offer the auto-login link.

**Deleting a bot** deactivates its user, the same way removing a person does: the user leaves every room (direct
rooms excepted), and its messages stay. The `bots` row is destroyed, which kills the bot code. Deactivated and
banned users fail authentication too (`Bot.active`).

**Posting.** `Bots::MessagesController` is unauthenticated by session and doesn't check CSRF tokens, because
the bot code in the path is the credential. Rails parses form bodies before any action runs, and it rejects
text such as `100% done` with a 400. The controller therefore declares the body as not being form fields
(`process_action`). `Bots::MessagesControllerTest` covers this.

**Authorization.** Editing and deleting use `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)`, which means administrator or
creator, the same rule used for other records here.

## Protecting bot codes

A bot code grants the ability to post as the bot, so:

- It's shown only on `/bots`, to the bot's creator and administrators. The edit page doesn't show it.
- `/bots` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`, so neither the browser nor

  URLs (`config/initializers/sentry.rb`).
- The code is generated by `has_secure_token` (24 base58 characters, about 140 bits) and is unique in the database.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# A bot is a user that a person set up to post messages over HTTP. Its name and avatar live on its user, so it
# shows up in rooms, mentions and messages exactly like a person. The bot key is the credential its API requests
# are authenticated with: it's only shown to the bot's creator and administrators, and it's masked in request logs and
# error reports.
class Bot < ApplicationRecord
  has_secure_token :bot_key

  belongs_to :user, autosave: true
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validates :name, presence: true

  scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).order("LOWER(users.name)") }
  scope :active, -> { joins(:user).merge(User.active) }
  scope :created_by, ->(user) { where(creator: user) }

  # Bot keys travel in the path of the message endpoint, so anything that records request paths (logs, error
  # reports) runs them through here to mask the key.
  def self.filter_path(path)
    path.sub(%r{(/rooms/[^/?]+/)[^/?]+(/messages)(?=\?|\z)}, '\1[FILTERED]\2')
  end

  def name
    user&.name
  end

  def name=(name)
    bot_user.name = name
  end

  def avatar=(avatar)
    bot_user.avatar = avatar
  end

  # Removing a bot keeps its messages, just as deactivating a person does, but its user stops being a member
  # of anything and its bot key stops working.
  def deactivate
    transaction do
      user.deactivate
      destroy!
    end
  end

  private
    # A bot never signs in, so nobody gets to know its password. The password digest column is required,
    # so the bot's user gets a random one that's thrown away.
    def bot_user
      user || build_user(password: SecureRandom.base58(64))
    end
end

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    # The page shows bot keys, so neither the browser nor anything in between should keep a copy.
    response.cache_control.merge!(no_store: true)

    @bots = (Current.user.can_administer? ? Bot.all : Bot.created_by(Current.user)).ordered.preload(:user)
  end

  def new
    @bot = Bot.new
  end

  def create
    Bot.create!(bot_params)

    redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @bot.update!(bot_params)

    redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate

    redirect_to bots_url
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.find(params[:id])
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)
    end

    # Browsers send an empty avatar field when no file was picked, which mustn't clear the existing avatar.
    def bot_params
      params.require(:bot).permit(:name, :avatar).compact
    end
end

# A bot is a user that a person set up to post messages over HTTP. Its name and avatar live on its user, so it
# shows up in rooms, mentions and messages exactly like a person. The bot key is the credential its API requests
# are authenticated with: it's only shown to the bot's creator and administrators, and it's masked in request logs and
# error reports.
class Bot < ApplicationRecord
  has_secure_token :bot_key

  belongs_to :user, autosave: true
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validates :name, presence: true

  scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).order("LOWER(users.name)") }
  scope :active, -> { joins(:user).merge(User.active) }
  scope :created_by, ->(user) { where(creator: user) }

  # Bot keys travel in the path of the message endpoint, so anything that records request paths (logs, error
  # reports) runs them through here to mask the key.
  def self.filter_path(path)
    path.sub(%r{(/rooms/[^/?]+/)[^/?]+(/messages)(?=\?|\z)}, '\1[FILTERED]\2')
  end

  def name
    user&.name
  end

  def name=(name)
    bot_user.name = name
  end

  def avatar=(avatar)
    bot_user.avatar = avatar
  end

  # Removing a bot keeps its messages, just as deactivating a person does, but its user stops being a member
  # of anything and its bot key stops working.
  def deactivate
    transaction do
      user.deactivate
      destroy!
    end
  end

  private
    # A bot never signs in, so nobody gets to know its password. The password digest column is required,
    # so the bot's user gets a random one that's thrown away.
    def bot_user
      user || build_user(password: SecureRandom.base58(64))
    end
end

  root "welcome#show"

  resource :first_run

  resource :session do
    scope module: "sessions" do
      resources :transfers, only: %i[ show update ]
    end
  end

  resource :account do
    scope module: "accounts" do
      resources :users

      resource :join_code, only: :create
      resource :logo, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :custom_styles, only: %i[ edit update ]
    end
  end

  direct :fresh_account_logo do |options|
    route_for :account_logo, v: Current.account&.updated_at&.to_fs(:number), size: options[:size]
  end

  get "join/:join_code", to: "users#new", as: :join
  post "join/:join_code", to: "users#create"

  resources :qr_code, only: :show

  resources :users, only: :show do
    scope module: "users" do
      resource :avatar, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :ban, only: %i[ create destroy ]

      scope defaults: { user_id: "me" } do
        resource :sidebar, only: :show
        resource :profile
        resources :push_subscriptions do
          scope module: "push_subscriptions" do
            resources :test_notifications, only: :create
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  namespace :autocompletable do
    resources :users, only: :index
  end

  direct :fresh_user_avatar do |user, options|
    route_for :user_avatar, user.avatar_token, v: user.updated_at.to_fs(:number)
  end

  resources :rooms do
    resources :messages

    scope module: "rooms" do
      resource :refresh, only: :show
      resource :settings, only: :show
      resource :involvement, only: %i[ show update ]
    end

    get "@:message_id", to: "rooms#show", as: :at_message
  end

  namespace :rooms do
    resources :opens
    resources :closeds
    resources :directs
  end

  resources :messages do
    scope module: "messages" do
      resources :boosts
    end
  end

  resources :bots, except: :show

  # Bots authenticate with the key in the path rather than a session, so this isn't nested under the rooms above.
  post "rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages", to: "bots/messages#create", as: :room_bot_messages

  resources :searches, only: %i[ index create ] do
    delete :clear, on: :collection
  end

  resource :unfurl_link, only: :create

  get "webmanifest"    => "pwa#manifest"
  get "service-worker" => "pwa#service_worker"

  get "up" => "rails/health#show", as: :rails_health_check
end

    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end

      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)

    end

class MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent, RoomScoped

  before_action :set_room, except: :create
  before_action :set_message, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  layout false, only: :index

  def index
    @messages = find_paged_messages

    if @messages.any?
      fresh_when @messages
    else
      head :no_content
    end
  end

  def create
    set_room
    @message = @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(message_params)

    @message.broadcast_create
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    render action: :room_not_found
  end

  def show
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @message.update!(message_params)

    @message.broadcast_replace_to @room, :messages, target: [ @message, :presentation ], partial: "messages/presentation", attributes: { maintain_scroll: true }

    redirect_to room_message_url(@room, @message)
  end

  def destroy
    @message.destroy
    @message.broadcast_remove
  end

  private
    def set_message
      @message = @room.messages.find(params[:id])
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@message)
    end


    def find_paged_messages
      case
      when params[:before].present?
        @room.messages.with_creator.page_before(@room.messages.find(params[:before]))
      when params[:after].present?
        @room.messages.with_creator.page_after(@room.messages.find(params[:after]))
      else
        @room.messages.with_creator.last_page
      end
    end


    def message_params
      params.require(:message).permit(:body, :attachment, :client_message_id)
    end
end

require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

class Opengraph::Fetch
  ALLOWED_DOCUMENT_CONTENT_TYPE = "text/html"
  MAX_BODY_SIZE = 5.megabytes
  MAX_REDIRECTS = 10

  class TooManyRedirectsError < StandardError; end
  class RedirectDeniedError < StandardError; end

  def fetch_document(url, ip: RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host))
    request(url, Net::HTTP::Get, ip: ip) do |response|
      return body_if_acceptable(response)
    end
  end

  def fetch_content_type(url, ip: RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host))
    request(url, Net::HTTP::Head, ip: ip) do |response|
      return response["Content-Type"]
    end
  end

  private
    def request(url, request_class, ip:)
      MAX_REDIRECTS.times do
        Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https") do |http|
          http.request request_class.new(url) do |response|
            if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPRedirection)
              url, ip = resolve_redirect(response["location"])
            else
              yield response
            end
          end
        end
      end

      raise TooManyRedirectsError
    end

    def resolve_redirect(location)
      url = URI.parse(location)
      raise RedirectDeniedError unless url.is_a?(URI::HTTP)
      [ url, RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host) ]
    end

    def body_if_acceptable(response)
      size_restricted_body(response) if response_valid?(response)
    end

    def size_restricted_body(response)
      # We've already checked the Content-Length header, to try to avoid reading
      # the body of any large responses. But that header could be wrong or
      # missing. To be on the safe side, we'll read the body in chunks, and bail
      # if it runs over our size limit.
      StringIO.new.tap do |body|
        response.read_body do |chunk|
          return nil if body.string.bytesize + chunk.bytesize > MAX_BODY_SIZE
          body << chunk
        end
      end.string
    end

    def response_valid?(response)
      status_valid?(response) && content_type_valid?(response) && content_length_valid?(response)
    end

    def status_valid?(response)
      response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)
    end

    def content_type_valid?(response)
      response.content_type == ALLOWED_DOCUMENT_CONTENT_TYPE
    end

    def content_length_valid?(response)
      response.content_length.to_i <= MAX_BODY_SIZE
    end
end

# This is in lib so we can use it in a thread pool without the Rails executor
class WebPush::Pool
  attr_reader :delivery_pool, :invalidation_pool, :connection, :invalid_subscription_handler

  def initialize(invalid_subscription_handler:)
    @delivery_pool = Concurrent::ThreadPoolExecutor.new(max_threads: 50, queue_size: 10000)
    @invalidation_pool = Concurrent::FixedThreadPool.new(1)
    @connection = Net::HTTP::Persistent.new(name: "web_push", pool_size: 150)
    @invalid_subscription_handler = invalid_subscription_handler
  end

  def queue(payload, subscriptions)
    subscriptions.find_each do |subscription|
      deliver_later(payload, subscription)
    end
  end

  def shutdown
    connection.shutdown
    shutdown_pool(delivery_pool)
    shutdown_pool(invalidation_pool)
  end

  private
    def deliver_later(payload, subscription)
      # Ensure any AR operations happen before we post to the thread pool
      notification = subscription.notification(**payload)
      subscription_id = subscription.id

      delivery_pool.post do
        deliver(notification, subscription_id)
      rescue Exception => e
        Rails.logger.error "Error in WebPush::Pool.deliver: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      end
    rescue Concurrent::RejectedExecutionError
    end

    def deliver(notification, id)
      notification.deliver(connection: connection)
    rescue WebPush::ExpiredSubscription, OpenSSL::OpenSSLError => ex
      invalidate_subscription_later(id) if invalid_subscription_handler
    end

    def invalidate_subscription_later(id)
      invalidation_pool.post do
        invalid_subscription_handler.call(id)
      rescue Exception => e
        Rails.logger.error "Error in WebPush::Pool.invalid_subscription_handler: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      end
    end

    def shutdown_pool(pool)
      pool.shutdown
      pool.kill unless pool.wait_for_termination(1)
    end
end

class WebPush::Notification
  def initialize(title:, body:, path:, badge:, endpoint:, p256dh_key:, auth_key:)
    @title, @body, @path, @badge = title, body, path, badge
    @endpoint, @p256dh_key, @auth_key = endpoint, p256dh_key, auth_key
  end

  def deliver(connection: nil)
    WebPush.payload_send \
      message: encoded_message,
      endpoint: @endpoint, p256dh: @p256dh_key, auth: @auth_key,
      vapid: vapid_identification,
      connection: connection,
      urgency: "high"
  end

  private
    def vapid_identification
      { subject: "mailto:support@37signals.com" }.merge \
        Rails.configuration.x.vapid.symbolize_keys
    end

    def encoded_message
      JSON.generate title: @title, options: { body: @body, icon: icon_path, data: { path: @path, badge: @badge } }
    end

    def icon_path
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.account_logo_path
    end
end

messages.content: The bot feature is mostly in place, and the uncommitted state is deliberate. Next I'll check the remaining bot tests, the bot-related helpers, and the environment (Ruby, bundle, and whether the test suite runs).

arguments.command: cd /app && cat lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path.rb; echo ----; cat test/models/bot_test.rb; echo ----; cat test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb; echo ----; cat test/controllers/bots/messages_controller_test.rb | head -150

messages.content: { "returncode": 0, "output_head": "# Rails masks only the query string when it logs a request path. The bot message endpoint carries its bot key in the # path, so the path is masked here too. That covers "Started POST" log lines and instrumentation. Error reports take # their URL from the request, so config/initializers/sentry.rb masks it there. module FilteredBotPath def filtered_path Bot.filter_path(super) end end ActionDispatch::Request.prepend FilteredBotPath ---- require "test_helper" class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase setup do @creator = users(:david) end test "creating a bot creates a user with its name, which is a bot" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.name assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.user.name assert bot.user.bot? assert_equal bot, bot.user.bot end test "creating a bot defaults the creator to the current user" do Current.set(user: @creator) do assert_equal @creator, Bot.create!(name: "Current Bot").creator end end test "a new bot joins every open room, like any new user" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count assert_not_includes bot.user.rooms, rooms(:watercooler) end test "a bot has a unique, unguessably long bot key" do first = Bot.create!(name: "First", creator: @creator) second = Bot.create!(name: "Second", creator: @creator) assert_operator first.bot_key.length, :>=, 24 assert_not_equal first.bot_key, second.bot_key end test "a bot needs a name" do bot = Bot.new(creator: @creator, name: "") assert_not bot.valid? assert bot.errors.of_kind?(:name, :blank) end test "renaming and changing the avatar go through the bot's user" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot", avatar: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open) assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bot.reload.user.name assert bot.user.avatar.attached? end test "a bot's user can't sign in, since nobody knows its password" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) assert_not bot.user.authenticate("secret123456") assert_nil User.active.authenticate_by(email_address: nil, password: "secret123456") end test "a person's user isn't a bot" do assert_not users(:david).bot? end test "deactivating a bot deactivates its user, removes it from rooms, and deletes its bot key" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) user = bot.user bot_key = bot.bot_key assert user.memberships.without_direct_rooms.any? bot.deactivate assert user.reload.deactivated? assert_equal 0, user.memberships.without_direct_rooms.count assert_not Bot.exists?(bot.id) assert_nil Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: bot_key) end test "only bots whose users are active can authenticate" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) assert_equal bot, Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: bot.bot_key) bot.user.update!(status: :banned) assert_nil Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: bot.bot_key) end test "the bot key is filtered out of the bot's inspected attributes" do bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator) assert_not_includes bot.inspect, bot.bot_key end end ---- require class ContentFilters::RemoveSoloUnfurledLinkText < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    normalize_tweet_url(solo_unfurled_url) == normalize_tweet_url(content.to_plain_text)
  end

  def apply
    fragment.replace("div") { |node| node.tap { |n| n.inner_html = unfurled_links.first.to_s } }
  end

  private
    TWITTER_DOMAINS = %w[ x.com twitter.com ]
    TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING = { "x.com" => "twitter.com" }

    def solo_unfurled_url
      unfurled_links.first["href"] if unfurled_links.size == 1
    end

    def unfurled_links
      fragment.find_all("action-text-attachment[@content-type='#{ActionText::Attachment::OpengraphEmbed::OPENGRAPH_EMBED_CONTENT_TYPE}']")
    end

    def normalize_tweet_url(url)
      return url unless twitter_url?(url)

      uri = URI.parse(url)

      uri.dup.tap do |u|
        u.host = TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING[uri.host&.downcase] || uri.host
        u.query = nil
      end.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      url
    end

    def twitter_url?(url)
      url.present? && TWITTER_DOMAINS.any? { |domain| url.strip.include?(domain) }
    end
end

class ContentFilters::SanitizeAttributes < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    true
  end

  # Scrub attributes on the tags that SanitizeTags allows, using Rails' safe-list
  # sanitizer so unsafe URI schemes and event-handler attributes are stripped.
  # Runs after SanitizeTags, so passing the same allowed tags makes the tag pass
  # a no-op and only attributes are scrubbed.
  def apply
    sanitizer.sanitize fragment.to_html, tags: allowed_tags, attributes: allowed_attributes
  end

  private
    # Presentation styling relies on class attributes (e.g. unfurled link embeds),
    # which the standard ActionText set doesn't include.
    EXTRA_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = %w[ class ]

    # ActionText::ContentHelper.sanitizer is a single process-wide instance, and
    # rails-html-sanitizer reuses one mutable permit scrubber that it reconfigures
    # from the tags/attributes on every #sanitize call. Sharing it here would race
    # our stricter tag set against ActionText's default rendering on concurrent
    # requests, so use a dedicated instance of the same sanitizer class to keep the
    # scrubber isolated.
    def sanitizer
      sanitizer_class.new
    end

    def sanitizer_class
      ActionText::ContentHelper.sanitizer.class
    end

    def allowed_tags
      ContentFilters::SanitizeTags::ALLOWED_TAGS
    end

    def allowed_attributes
      standard_allowed_attributes + EXTRA_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES
    end

    # Mirrors ActionText::ContentHelper#sanitizer_allowed_attributes, which isn't
    # exposed at the module level.
    def standard_allowed_attributes
      ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_attributes ||
        (sanitizer_class.allowed_attributes + ActionText::Attachment::ATTRIBUTES).to_a
    end
end

class ContentFilters::SanitizeTags < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?

  end

  def apply

      p pre samp small span strong sub sup time tt ul var ] + [ ActionText::Attachment.tag_name, "figure", "figcaption" ]

class Rooms::DirectsController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ edit destroy ]
  def new
    @room = Rooms::Direct.new
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(selected_users)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
  end

  private
    def selected_users
      User.where(id: selected_users_ids.including(Current.user.id))
    end

    def selected_users_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      room.memberships.each do |membership|
        membership.broadcast_prepend_to membership.user, :rooms, target: :direct_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/direct"
      end
    end

    # All users in a direct room can administer it. Only direct rooms, though: this
    # relaxation is why room_scope below has to keep every other type out of reach.
    def ensure_can_administer
      true
    end

    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.directs
    end
end

class Rooms::DirectsController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ edit destroy ]
  def new
    @room = Rooms::Direct.new
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(selected_users)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
  end

  private
    def selected_users
      User.where(id: selected_users_ids.including(Current.user.id))
    end

    def selected_users_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      room.memberships.each do |membership|
        membership.broadcast_prepend_to membership.user, :rooms, target: :direct_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/direct"
      end
    end

    # All users in a direct room can administer it. Only direct rooms, though: this
    # relaxation is why room_scope below has to keep every other type out of reach.
    def ensure_can_administer
      true
    end

    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.directs
    end
end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "  NAT64_LOCAL_USE = IPAddr.new("64:ff9b:1::/48")  # RFC 8215

  # SIIT's IPv4-translated form is the third way an IPv4 address rides inside an
  # IPv6 one, and the only one Ruby has no predicate for: ipv4_mapped?,
  # ipv4_compat?, private?, loopback? and link_local? are all false for
  # ::ffff:0:169.254.169.254, so it would reach the metadata address straight
  # through the branches below. Note the extra group — ::ffff:0:0:0/96 is NOT the
  # familiar IPv4-mapped ::ffff:0:0/96, and the two ranges do not overlap. Like
  # the NAT64 well-known prefix it is a fixed /96, so decode the low 32 bits.
  IPV4_TRANSLATABLE = IPAddr.new("::ffff:0:0:0/96") # RFC 2765

  # Every PUBLIC address the host resolves to, IPv4 ahead of IPv6, DNS order
  # preserved within each family so a provider's round-robin still spreads load.
  # Empty when the host resolves but every address is blocked; raises
  # Unresolvable when it resolves to nothing at all, so the caller can tell a
  # refusal from a lookup failure. A caller that fails over MUST iterate this
  # list and pin each address; resolving again reopens the rebinding window.
  # Accepts a hostname or an IP-literal host.
  def resolve_public_ips(host)
    addresses = resolve(host)
    raise Unresolvable, "No address for #{host}" if addresses.empty?

    addresses.reject { |ip| blocked_address?(ip) }
             .partition(&:ipv4?)
             .flatten
             .map(&:to_s)
  end

  # True only if the URL's host resolves to at least one address and NONE are
  # blocked. For non-pinning callers (they hand the hostname straight to
  # Net::HTTP, which resolves again), so anything short of "every address is
  # public" is unsafe. A predicate answers the question it was asked and doesn't
  # raise: false covers unresolvable and malformed alike. Reach for
  # .enforce_public_ip or .resolve_public_ip when you need to tell those apart.
  def resolvable_public_ip?(url)
    addresses = resolve(host_of(url))
    addresses.any? && addresses.none? { |ip| blocked_address?(ip) }
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError, IPAddr::InvalidAddressError, ArgumentError
    false

- **Storage:** `webhook_url` column on `bots` (done), normalized so blank means "no webhook", and validated as http(s).
- **Trigger:** `Room#receive` (already the post-commit hook) enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per mentioned bot that has a webhook. Only people's messages trigger, so bots can't loop.

- **Reply:** 200 with `text/plain`/`text/html` is posted as the bot's message (HTML is sanitized, and mentions/attachments are stripped). Anything else posts nothing.

require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Tells a bot's webhook about a mention, and posts the bot's answer into the room when it gives one.
#
# The webhook is asked with a JSON POST. The answer is in the HTTP response:
#
# - 200 with a text/plain or text/html body: the body is posted into the room as the bot's message.
# - 204, or any other response: nothing is posted. Redirects aren't followed.
#
# Webhook URLs are set by members, so they're fetched the way link unfurling fetches URLs: addresses that are private
# or internal are refused, and the checked address is the one connected to, so a DNS change can't redirect the request.
#
# This runs in a job, so the person who posted the message never waits on the bot.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds to connect
  READ_TIMEOUT = 15 # seconds between reads
  DEADLINE = 30 # seconds for the whole exchange, so a bot can't drip out its answer and hold a worker

  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  # Ways a webhook can fail that aren't a bug here: refused addresses, unreachable or misbehaving servers, and
  # responses that can't be read. Anything else is left to raise, so it reaches the job's error reporting.
  FAILURES = [
    RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable, URI::InvalidURIError, Timeout::Error,
    SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse,
    Net::HTTPHeaderSyntaxError, Zlib::Error
  ]

  # Content from a bot is sanitized the same way as the room's messages. The same filters run when a message is
  # displayed, so storing clean content doesn't change what people see.
  SANITIZE = ActionText::Content::Filters.new(ContentFilters::SanitizeTags, ContentFilters::SanitizeAttributes)

  attr_reader :bot, :message, :room

  def initialize(bot, message)
    @bot, @message, @room = bot, message, message.room
  end

  def deliver
    return unless bot.user.active? && bot.webhook_url

    reply = fetch_reply
    post_reply(*reply) if reply
  rescue *FAILURES => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} failed without a reply: #{e.class}"
  end

  # The JSON sent to the webhook. Paths are relative: the bot knows its Campfire origin.
  def payload
    {
      event: "mention",
      author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name },
      room: { id: room.id, name: room_name, reply_to: routes.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key) },
      message: {
        id: message.id,
        body: { text: text, html: html },
        link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
      }
    }
  end

  private
    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end

    def uri
      @uri ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    def room_name
      if room.direct?
        room.users.where.not(id: bot.user_id).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence || bot.name
      else
        room.name
      end
    end

    # The message as text, with this bot's own @mention taken out, so that it reads as the command addressed to the bot.
    def text
      @text ||= content_without_bot_mention.to_plain_text.gsub(/[ \t]{2,}/, " ").strip
    end

    def content_without_bot_mention
      fragment = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot.user ? nil : node
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false)
    end

    # The whole message as rich text, mentions included.
    def html
      @html ||= SANITIZE.apply(message.body.body).to_html
    end

    # Returns [content type, text] for an answer that should be posted, or nil.
    def fetch_reply
      Timeout.timeout(DEADLINE) do
        address = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.host)

        Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, ipaddr: address, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
            open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http|
          http.request(post_request) do |response|
            # Returning from inside the block leaves the response unread, so a large or endless body isn't downloaded.
            return reply_from(response)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def post_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def reply_from(response)
      content_type = response.content_type.to_s.downcase

      return unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK) && REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(content_type)

      if body = read_capped_body(response)
        [ content_type, decode(body, response.type_params["charset"]) ]
      end
    end

    # Nil if the body is larger than a reply can be.
    def read_capped_body(response)
      body = String.new

      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        return if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      body
    end

    # The body as UTF-8 text, or nil when it isn't valid in its charset. A reply that doesn't name one is UTF-8.
    def decode(body, charset)
      text = body.force_encoding(charset || Encoding::UTF_8).encode(Encoding::UTF_8)
      text if text.valid_encoding?
    rescue EncodingError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    def post_reply(content_type, text)
      return if text.nil?

      # The bot may have left the room while its webhook was answering.
      return unless room.users.exists?(bot.user_id)

      if content_type == "text/html"
        post_html_reply(text)
      else
        post_text_reply(text)
      end
    end

    def post_text_reply(text)
      text = text.strip
      bot.post_text(room, text) if text.present?
    end

    def post_html_reply(html)
      content = sanitized_reply(html)
      bot.post_html(room, content.to_html) if content.to_plain_text.present?
    end

    # A bot's HTML is posted without attachments. A mention or other attachment would notify people, and trigger
    # bots, as though a person had written it.
    def sanitized_reply(html)
      fragment = ActionText::Fragment.from_html(html).replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) { nil }

      SANITIZE.apply(ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false))
    end
end
EOF

# The bot message API. A bot posts by sending the message text as the raw request body, e.g.
#
#   curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-key>/messages
#
# There is no session here: the bot key in the path is the credential.
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :set_room

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    head :not_found
  end

  def create
    text = message_text
    return head :unprocessable_content unless text

    @message = @bot.post_text(@room, text)

    head :created, location: message_path(@message)
  end

  # Clients send curl's default form encoding, and Rails would try to parse the body as form fields before the
  # action runs, rejecting text such as "100% done". The body is the message, so it's never read as fields.
  def process_action(...)
    request.request_parameters = {}
    super
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: params[:bot_key])

      unless @bot
        response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] = %(Bot realm="Campfire")
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.user.rooms.find(params[:room_id])
    end

    # The body as text, stripped. Nil when it's blank or isn't valid UTF-8, which both count as an empty message.
    def message_text
      text = String.new(request.raw_post, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
      text.strip if text.valid_encoding? && text.present?
    end
end

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    # The page shows bot keys, so neither the browser nor anything in between should keep a copy.
    response.cache_control.merge!(no_store: true)

    @bots = (Current.user.can_administer? ? Bot.all : Bot.created_by(Current.user)).ordered.preload(:user)
  end

  def new
    @bot = Bot.new
  end

  def create
    Bot.create!(bot_params)

    redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
  end

  def edit
    # The page shows the webhook URL, which can carry a secret of its own, so it's kept out of caches too.
    response.cache_control.merge!(no_store: true)
  end

  def update
    @bot.update!(bot_params)

    redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate

    redirect_to bots_url
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.find(params[:id])
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)

messages.content: That passes. Before moving on, I want to revisit one design point. `Room#receive` currently looks up mentioned bots in the request, which means extra DB queries on the posting path, and the spec says posting must never be slowed. The existing `push_later` pattern already handles this: the request enqueues one job and the job decides who to notify. I'll follow that exactly, with a `Room::AskMentionedBotsJob` that does the lookup and fans out one `Bot::WebhookJob` per bot.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/jobs/room/ask_mentioned_bots_job.rb <<'EOF'
class Room::AskMentionedBotsJob < ApplicationJob
  # The message may be deleted before the job runs. Then there's no one left to ask.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  # Each bot gets a job of its own, so a slow webhook doesn't hold up the others.
  def perform(message)
    message.mentioned_bots.each do |bot|
      Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, message)
    end
  end
end
EOF
ruby -e '
p = "app/models/room.rb"
s = File.read(p)
old1 = "    push_later(message)\n    ask_mentioned_bots_later(message)\n  end\n"
new1 = "    push_later(message)\n    ask_mentioned_bots_later(message)\n  end\n"
old2 = "    def ask_mentioned_bots_later(message)\n      message.mentioned_bots.each do |bot|\n        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, message)\n      end\n    end\n"
new2 = "    def ask_mentioned_bots_later(message)\n      Room::AskMentionedBotsJob.perform_later(message)\n    end\n"
raise "old2" unless s.scan(old2).size == 1
File.write(p, s.sub(old2, new2))
puts "ok"' && git diff -- app/models/room.rb

messages.content: All 28 pass. Next is a real-network check that WebMock can't give me: `Net::HTTP` with the pinned `ipaddr` against a live local server. The guard blocks loopback by design, so in this scratch test I'll stub only the DNS-guard resolution and leave everything else real. It'll cover a text reply, an HTML reply, a 204, a redirect, an oversized body, and a hanging server.

arguments.command:
cd /app && mkdir -p test/scratch && cat > test/scratch/e2e_test.rb <<'EOF' require "test_helper" require "socket" class E2EScratchTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase setup do WebMock.allow_net_connect! @requests = Queue.new @server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", 0) @port = @server.addr[1] @thread = Thread.new do loop do client = @server.accept rescue break Thread.new(client) do |sock| begin request_line = sock.gets headers = {} while (line = sock.gets) && line != "\r\n" k, v = line.split(": ", 2) headers[k.downcase] = v.to_s.strip end body = headers["content-length"] ? sock.read(headers["content-length"].to_i) : "" path = request_line.split(" ")[1] @requests << { path: path, headers: headers, body: body } case path when "/text" respond(sock, "200 OK", "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "Build #1 is & \"done\"\n\nSee you") when "/html" respond(sock, "200 OK", "text/html", "
Hi there
") when "/nothing" sock.write "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n" when "/redirect" sock.write "HTTP/1.1 302 Found\r\nLocation: http://127.0.0.1:1/elsewhere\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n" when "/huge" respond(sock, "200 OK", "text/plain", "x" * 200_000) when "/hang" sleep 60 when "/json" respond(sock, "200 OK", "application/json", "{}") end rescue => e @requests << { error: e.class.name } ensure sock.close rescue nil end end end end RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.stubs(:resolve).returns("127.0.0.1") end teardown do @server.close rescue nil @thread.kill WebMock.disable_net_connect! end def respond(sock, status, type, body) sock.write "HTTP/1.1 #{status}\r\nContent-Type: #{type}\r\nContent-Length: #{body.bytesize}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n#{body}" end def bot_for(path) Bot.create!(name: "Echo Bot #{path}", creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "http://hooks.example.test:#{@port}#{path}") end def mention(user) mention_attachment_for(user) end test "text reply, html reply, 204, redirect, json, huge, hang" do room = rooms(:hq) results = {} %w[ /text /html /nothing /redirect /json /huge ].each do |path| bot = bot_for(path) room.memberships.grant_to(bot.user) message = room.messages.create!(creator: users(:jason), body: "

") before = Message.count started = Time.now Bot::Webhook.new(bot, message).deliver results[path] = { new_messages: Message.count - before, seconds: (Time.now - started).round(2) } last = Message.order(:id).last results[path][:posted] = last.plain_text_body if Message.count > before results[path][:posted_html] = last.body.body.to_html if Message.count > before end puts "RESULTS: #{results.inspect}" req = nil req = @requests.pop until (req = @requests.pop(true) rescue nil).nil? ? false : true end test "hang is cut off by the deadline" do Bot::Webhook.send(:remove_const, :DEADLINE) rescue nil Bot::Webhook.const_set(:DEADLINE, 3) room = rooms(:hq) bot = bot_for("/hang") room.memberships.grant_to(bot.user) message = room.messages.create!(creator: users(:jason), body: "
#{mention(bot.user)} hi

require "test_helper"
require "capybara/cuprite"

Capybara.register_driver :scratch_cuprite do |app|
  Capybara::Cuprite::Driver.new(app, browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", window_size: [ 1400, 1400 ], headless: true,
    process_timeout: 60, timeout: 30, browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil })
end

class ScratchBotBrowserTest < ActionDispatch::SystemTestCase
  setup do
    WebMock.disable!
    Capybara.current_driver = :scratch_cuprite
    Capybara.server = :puma, { Silent: true }
  end

  teardown do
    Capybara.use_default_driver
    WebMock.enable!
  end

  test "bot form: webhook URL field, save, clear, native confirm delete, and @ autocomplete" do
    visit root_url
    fill_in "email_address", with: "david@37signals.com"
    fill_in "password", with: "secret123456"
    click_on "log_in"
    assert_selector "a.btn", text: "HQ"

    visit new_bot_url
    puts "NEW FORM LABELS: #{page.all("label").map(&:text).inspect}"
    puts "WEBHOOK FIELD: #{find_field("Webhook URL")[:type]} placeholder=#{find_field("Webhook URL")[:placeholder].inspect}"
    fill_in "Name the bot", with: "Echo Bot"
    fill_in "Webhook URL", with: "https://hooks.example.com/echo"
    click_on "Save changes"
    assert_current_path bots_path
    assert_selector "#bots strong", text: "Echo Bot"
    puts "AFTER CREATE: list shows Echo Bot"

    click_link "Edit Echo Bot"
    puts "EDIT FIELD VALUE: #{find_field("Webhook URL").value.inspect}"
    assert_equal "https://hooks.example.com/echo", find_field("Webhook URL").value

    fill_in "Webhook URL", with: ""
    click_on "Save changes"
    assert_current_path bots_path
    click_link "Edit Echo Bot"
    puts "AFTER CLEAR VALUE: #{find_field("Webhook URL").value.inspect}"
    assert_equal "", find_field("Webhook URL").value

    fill_in "Webhook URL", with: "not a url"
    click_on "Save changes"
    puts "INVALID URL STAYED ON FORM: #{current_path} (browser validation for type=url)"
    fill_in "Webhook URL", with: "https://hooks.example.com/echo"
    click_on "Save changes"

    click_link "Edit Echo Bot"
    accept_confirm("Are you sure you want to delete this chat bot? It won’t be able to post messages anymore, and this can’t be undone.") do
      click_on "Delete this chat bot"
    end
    assert_current_path bots_path
    assert_no_selector "#bots strong", text: "Echo Bot"
    puts "NATIVE CONFIRM DELETE: OK"

    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Echo Bot", creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://hooks.example.com/echo")
    rooms(:hq).memberships.grant_to(bot.user)

    visit room_url(rooms(:hq))
    assert_selector "trix-editor"
    find("trix-editor").click
    find("trix-editor").send_keys "@Ech"
    assert_selector ".autocomplete__item .autocompletable__name", text: "Echo Bot", wait: 10
    puts "AUTOCOMPLETE SHOWS BOT: yes"
  end
end
EOF

EOF cat > /tmp/doc_webhooks.txt <<'EOF' ## Receiving mentions (webhooks) A bot can have a **webhook URL**, set in the "Webhook URL" field on `/bots/new` or the bot's edit page. When a person mentions the bot (`@Deploy Bot`) in a message, Campfire POSTs the mention to that URL. The bot answers either in the HTTP response, or later by posting through its bot code. Leaving the field empty removes the webhook. The request is `POST ` with `Content-Type: application/json`: ```json { "event": "mention", "author": { "id": 7, "name": "Alice" }, "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5//messages" }, "message": { "id": 118, "body": { "text": "restart the build please", "html": "
… full rich-text body …
" }, "link": "/rooms/5/@118" } } ``` - `event` is always `mention` for now. More event types may come later. - `message.body.text` is the message as text, with the bot's own @mention taken out, so it reads as the command addressed to the bot. Other mentions read as `@Name`. - `message.body.html` is the whole rich-text body, cleaned the way the room cleans messages. Mentions are `action-text-attachment` elements, and their `sgid` identifies the person mentioned. - `room.reply_to` is the bot's own posting URL for that room. POST text to it to reply later (see "Posting messages"). - `message.link` opens the room scrolled to the message. - Paths are relative. The bot knows its Campfire origin, so `https://chat.example.com` plus `reply_to` is the URL. - In a direct message room, `room.name` is the other people in it. The bot replies with: | Response | Result | | --- | --- | | `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` | The body is posted into the room as the bot's message. Line breaks are kept and markup is shown as text. | | `200` with `Content-Type: text/html` | The body is posted as the bot's rich text. Scripts, images and other tags the room doesn't display are removed, and so are mentions and other attachments. | | `204` | Nothing is posted. | | Anything else | Nothing is posted. Redirects aren't followed. | A `200` body that is blank posts nothing. A body over 64 KB posts nothing (it isn't truncated). A charset in `Content-Type` is honoured, and a body that isn't valid text in its charset posts nothing. Timing and failures: - Webhooks are called from a background job, so posting a message never waits on a bot. An answer appears a moment after the mention. - The bot has 5 seconds to connect, 15 seconds between reads, and 30 seconds for the whole exchange. - A webhook that fails, times out or is refused posts nothing. Failures are logged without the URL or the payload. There are no retries. What asks a webhook: - A mention of the bot in a message that a person posts, while the bot is a member of that room. A closed room needs access granted first, as for people. - Only the bot's messages are not asked: a bot's own message never asks another bot, so two bots can't keep each other talking. Bot replies can't mention anyone anyway (see below). - Only when the message is posted. Editing a message to add a mention doesn't ask, the same as push notifications. - Never when the bot has no webhook URL. Webhook URLs must be `http` or `https`. Campfire fetches webhooks the same way it fetches links for unfurling, so addresses that are private or internal (loopback, private networks, link-local) are refused. A webhook on the same private network as Campfire doesn't work today. See "Known limits". EOF cat > /tmp/doc_design.txt <<'EOF' **Webhooks.** `Room#receive` enqueues `Room::AskMentionedBotsJob` for each new message, the same way it enqueues push notifications. That job finds the mentioned bots (`Message#mentioned_bots`) and enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per bot, so one slow webhook doesn't hold up the others. `Bot::Webhook` builds the payload, makes the request and posts the answer. Nothing on the posting request's path talks to a webhook, and the job arguments are GlobalIDs, so the queue never holds a payload or a bot code. **Fetching webhooks** uses `RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard`, as link unfurling does (see `SECURITY.md`: any member can make Campfire fetch a URL, so the destination is checked). The checked address is pinned with `ipaddr:`, so a DNS change between the check and the connection can't move the request to an internal host. Redirects aren't followed, the body is read only up to 64 KB, and a `Timeout` caps the whole exchange, so a bot can't keep a worker busy by dripping bytes slowly. **Answers from bots** go through the same sanitizing filters the room uses on display (`ContentFilters::SanitizeTags` and `SanitizeAttributes`) before they're stored, and all `action-text-attachment` elements are removed first. An attachment in a bot's answer would notify the person it names as if they had written it, so bots can't create mentions. **The bot code in the payload.** `room.reply_to` contains the bot code, so the webhook's recipient learns it. That's intended: the webhook is the bot. It's the only place the code leaves Campfire, and the payload is never logged. **Webhook URLs are secrets** (they often carry a token in the path or query). The parameter filter masks `webhook_url` in request logs and in `inspect`, and the bot's edit page isn't cached. EOF cat > /tmp/doc_limits.txt <<'EOF' Known limits (webhooks): - Private and internal webhook addresses are refused, so a bot whose service runs on the same private network as Campfire can't use a webhook yet. Allowing them would be a deliberate, per-deployment decision. - Requests aren't signed, so the webhook URL is the only secret. A receiver can't tell a genuine mention from a forged POST unless the URL is secret. - There are no retries and no delivery log. A failed webhook is only logged, by class. - Sentry's HTTP breadcrumbs record a webhook's scheme, host and path (not its query) when an error is reported after a webhook call. They go to the operator's own `SENTRY_DSN`. - Replies over 64 KB are dropped, not truncated. - Edits that add a mention don't ask the bot. (`ContentFilters::SanitizeTags` and `SanitizeAttributes`) before they're stored, and all `action-text-attachment`
elements are removed first. An attachment in a bot's answer would notify the person it names as if they had written
it, so bots can't create mentions.

**The bot code in the payload.** `room.reply_to` contains the bot code, so the webhook's recipient learns it. That's
intended: the webhook is the bot. It's the only place the code leaves Campfire, and the payload is never logged.

**Webhook URLs are secrets** (they often carry a token in the path or query). The parameter filter masks
`webhook_url` in request logs and in `inspect`, and the bot's edit page isn't cached.

**Authorization.** Editing and deleting use `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)`, which means administrator or
creator, the same rule used for other records here.

## Protecting bot codes

A bot code grants the ability to post as the bot, so:

- It's shown only on `/bots`, to the bot's creator and administrators. The edit page doesn't show it.
- `/bots` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`, so neither the browser nor
  Turbo's page cache keeps a copy.
- It never appears in messages, broadcasts, redirects, flash messages or JSON.
- Rails' parameter filter masks it (`bot_key` matches the existing `_key` filter), so `Parameters:` log lines show
  `[FILTERED]`.
- Rails masks only the query string when it logs a path, so `lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path.rb` masks the code in
  the path too: `Started POST "/rooms/1/[FILTERED]/messages"`. `Bot.filter_path` does the same for Sentry request
  URLs (`config/initializers/sentry.rb`).
- The code is generated by `has_secure_token` (24 base58 characters, about 140 bits) and is unique in the database.

Known limits:

- The code is stored in plain text, because the page has to show it again. Anyone with database access can read it.
- ActiveRecord's SQL debug logging prints the value in the `bots.bot_key` query, in development or with
  `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`. Session tokens already appear the same way. Production logs at `info` by default.
- Reverse-proxy access logs record the full path, which includes the code. Treat those logs as sensitive.

Not built yet: rotating a bot code (`regenerate_bot_key` is available), rate limiting failed code attempts,
per-bot scopes, and a size limit on message bodies (any size is accepted today).

- `app/controllers/bots/messages_controller.rb` (the posting API)

require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Tells a bot's webhook about a mention, and posts the bot's answer into the room when it gives one.
#
# The webhook is asked with a JSON POST. The answer is in the HTTP response:
#
# - 200 with a text/plain or text/html body: the body is posted into the room as the bot's message.
# - 204, or any other response: nothing is posted. Redirects aren't followed.
#
# Webhook URLs are set by members, so they're fetched the way link unfurling fetches URLs: addresses that are private
# or internal are refused, and the checked address is the one connected to, so a DNS change can't redirect the request.
#
# This runs in a job, so the person who posted the message never waits on the bot.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds to connect
  READ_TIMEOUT = 15 # seconds between reads
  DEADLINE = 30 # seconds for the whole exchange, so a bot can't drip out its answer and hold a worker

  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  # Ways a webhook can fail that aren't a bug here: refused addresses, unreachable or misbehaving servers, and
  # responses that can't be read. Anything else is left to raise, so it reaches the job's error reporting.
  FAILURES = [
    RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable, URI::InvalidURIError, Timeout::Error,
    SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse,
    Net::HTTPHeaderSyntaxError, Zlib::Error
  ]

  # Content from a bot is sanitized the same way as the room's messages. The same filters run when a message is
  # displayed, so storing clean content doesn't change what people see.
  SANITIZE = ActionText::Content::Filters.new(ContentFilters::SanitizeTags, ContentFilters::SanitizeAttributes)

  attr_reader :bot, :message, :room

  def initialize(bot, message)
    @bot, @message, @room = bot, message, message.room
  end

  def deliver
    return unless bot.user.active? && bot.webhook_url

    reply = fetch_reply
    post_reply(*reply) if reply
  rescue *FAILURES => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} failed without a reply: #{e.class}"
  end

  # The JSON sent to the webhook. Paths are relative: the bot knows its Campfire origin.
  def payload
    {
      event: "mention",
      author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name },
      room: { id: room.id, name: room_name, reply_to: routes.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key) },
      message: {
        id: message.id,
        body: { text: text, html: html },
        link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
      }
    }
  end

  private
    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end

    def uri
      @uri ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    def room_name
      if room.direct?
        room.users.where.not(id: bot.user_id).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence || bot.name
      else
        room.name
      end
    end

    # The message as text, with this bot's own @mention taken out, so that it reads as the command addressed to the bot.
    def text
      @text ||= content_without_bot_mention.to_plain_text.gsub(/[ \t]{2,}/, " ").strip
    end

    def content_without_bot_mention
      fragment = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot.user ? nil : node
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false)
    end

    # The whole message as rich text, mentions included.
    def html
      @html ||= SANITIZE.apply(message.body.body).to_html
    end

    # Returns [content type, text] for an answer that should be posted, or nil.
    def fetch_reply
      Timeout.timeout(DEADLINE) do
        address = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.host)

        Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, ipaddr: address, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
            open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http|
          http.request(post_request) do |response|
            # Returning from inside the block leaves the response unread, so a large or endless body isn't downloaded.
            return reply_from(response)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def post_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def reply_from(response)
      content_type = response.content_type.to_s.downcase

      return unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK) && REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(content_type)

      if body = read_capped_body(response)
        [ content_type, decode(body, response.type_params["charset"]) ]
      end
    end

    # Nil if the body is larger than a reply can be.
    def read_capped_body(response)
      body = String.new

      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        return if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      body
    end

    # The body as UTF-8 text, or nil when it isn't valid in its charset. A reply that doesn't name one is UTF-8.
    def decode(body, charset)
      text = body.force_encoding(charset || Encoding::UTF_8).encode(Encoding::UTF_8)
      text if text.valid_encoding?
    rescue EncodingError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    def post_reply(content_type, text)
      return if text.nil?

      # The bot may have left the room while its webhook was answering.
      return unless room.users.exists?(bot.user_id)

      if content_type == "text/html"
        post_html_reply(text)
      else
        post_text_reply(text)
      end
    end

    def post_text_reply(text)
      text = text.strip
      bot.post_text(room, text) if text.present?
    end

    def post_html_reply(html)
      content = sanitized_reply(html)
      bot.post_html(room, content.to_html) if content.to_plain_text.present?
    end

    # A bot's HTML is posted without attachments. A mention or other attachment would notify people, and trigger
    # bots, as though a person had written it.
    def sanitized_reply(html)
      fragment = ActionText::Fragment.from_html(html).replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) { nil }

      SANITIZE.apply(ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false))
    end
end

The class reads correctly, but I see two robustness gaps:

1. **`Zlib::Error` in `FAILURES`:** the constant is referenced at class-load time. It works here, but I'd rather not depend on something else having loaded zlib, so I'll require it explicitly.
2. **IPv6 literal hosts:** `URI#host` keeps the brackets (`[2606:4700::1111]`), which the guard can't parse, so a public IPv6 webhook would be refused. `URI#hostname` strips them, so I'll use that.

{ "returncode": 0, "output": " ## Receiving mentions (webhooks) A bot can have a **webhook URL**, set in the "Webhook URL" field on `/bots/new` or the bot's edit page. When a person mentions the bot (`@Deploy Bot`) in a message, Campfire POSTs the mention to that URL. The bot answers either in the HTTP response, or later by posting through its bot code. Leaving the field empty removes the webhook. The request is `POST ` with `Content-Type: application/json`: ```json { "event": "mention", "author": { "id": 7, "name": "Alice" }, "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5//messages" }, "message": { "id": 118, "body": { "text": "restart the build please", "html": "
… full rich-text body …
" }, "link": "/rooms/5/@118" } } ``` - `event` is always `mention` for now. More event types may come later. - `message.body.text` is the message as text, with the bot's own @mention taken out, so it reads as the command addressed to the bot. Other mentions read as `@Name`. - `message.body.html` is the whole rich-text body, cleaned the way the room cleans messages. Mentions are `action-text-attachment` elements, and their `sgid` identifies the person mentioned. - `room.reply_to` is the bot's own posting URL for that room. POST text to it to reply later (see "Posting messages"). - `message.link` opens the room scrolled to the message. - Paths are relative. The bot knows its Campfire origin, so `https://chat.example.com` plus `reply_to` is the URL. - In a direct message room, `room.name` is the other people in it. messages.content:
The feature is implemented and verified. Before submitting, here's the state of the work.

## Summary

Bots can now have an optional **Webhook URL**. When someone mentions a bot, Campfire POSTs a JSON payload to it. The bot can answer in the response (200 `text/plain` or `text/html` posts a message, 204 posts nothing) or later through its existing posting URL.

**What changed**
- **Storage and form:** `webhook_url` column on `bots`. The field is labelled "Webhook URL" on both `/bots/new` and the edit page. It's validated as http(s), and an empty value clears the webhook.
- **Trigger:** `Room#receive` enqueues `Room::AskMentionedBotsJob`, which finds mentioned bots and enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per bot. The posting request makes no webhook calls.
- **Delivery:** `Bot::Webhook` builds the payload (`text` with the bot's own mention removed, rich-text `html`, relative `reply_to` and `link`) and handles the response. Its failure handling covers timeouts, refusals, and redirects.
- **Docs:** `docs/bots.md` has a webhook section, design notes, and known limits.

**Decisions to review**
- **Webhooks go through the SSRF guard**, like link unfurling. Per `SECURITY.md`, any member can make the server fetch a URL, so private and loopback addresses are refused. **This matters for QA:** a receiver on localhost won't get callbacks. Relaxing this is your call.
- **Only people's messages ask bots**, so two bots can't loop. Bot replies are sanitized, and mention attachments are stripped so bots can't ping people.
- **Edits don't trigger webhooks**, matching push notifications.
- **Limits:** 5s connect, 15s reads, 30s total. Redirects aren't followed. Replies are capped at 64 KB, and there are no retries.
- **Logging:** the webhook URL is masked in parameter logs, and the edit page isn't cached.
- **Bot posting** now goes through `Bot#post_text`, shared with the existing API. Its behavior is unchanged.

**Deviations from the spec's example**
- `reply_to` uses the existing bot posting route, `/rooms/:id/<bot_key>/messages`. The spec's sample segment (`42-Xy3abc9defGh`) doesn't match the 24-character key format.
- `message.body.html` is the stored rich-text HTML with mentions as `action-text-attachment` elements, not the room's rendered markup.

**Verification**
- Full suite: 414 runs, 0 failures. The 22 skips are DNS-dependent tests that also skip on the untouched baseline.
- Real-network check, bypassing WebMock with a live local server: text reply, HTML reply, 204, redirect, oversized body, and a hanging server cut off at the deadline.
- Browser check via Cuprite and the system Chromium, using a scratch test that I removed. It confirmed the field labels, create/edit/clear, the native `confirm()` on delete, and that `@` autocomplete shows the bot.
- RuboCop and Brakeman are clean, and eager loading works.

The bot feature was already partly built and uncommitted in the working tree; I built on top of it and didn't commit anything. While rewriting `bot.rb` I briefly mangled the `filter_path` regex. I caught it and restored the original bytes before finishing.
